hiw.hero.sub: Each step happens on its own page. Nothing demands more than one decision from you at a time.
hiw.step1.title: Confirm safety.
hiw.step1.body: Age attestation comes first. Adults continue privately. If you are under 18, Asmita does not collect URLs - it routes you to CHILDLINE 1098, TakeItDown, and cybercrime.gov.in with guided instructions.
hiw.step2.title: Paste links as text.
hiw.step2.body: Asmita reads only the domain string from each URL to route the notice to the right platform. The link itself never reaches the server, and no one at Asmita or the grievance officer can access or view the content it points to. Up to ten URLs every twenty-four hours.
hiw.step3.title: Fingerprint the image, not the image itself.
hiw.step3.body: If you choose to submit a hash, a perceptual fingerprint is computed entirely on your device. A 64-character code is what leaves your browser - the original image never touches the server, and neither Asmita nor any grievance officer can reconstruct or view it from that code. The fingerprint is shared with platforms that support proactive blocking so they can detect and prevent re-uploads.
hiw.step4.title: Reviewed notices go out.
hiw.step4.body: Platform contacts are human-verified before they enter the routing table. You approve every notice before it is sent. When a notice is dispatched, the grievance officer receives a secure link protected by a one-time password. The link burns after it is opened once and cannot be revisited.
hiw.step5.title: Submit the form yourself, with everything ready.
hiw.step5.body: For platforms with no grievance officer contact, Asmita prepares a step-by-step handoff. The notice text, your PDQ fingerprint if applicable, and the exact form URL are all ready. You paste, submit, and Asmita logs it.
hiw.step6.title: Track and escalate.
hiw.step6.body: A private dashboard shows each platform, the response window, and an audit trail. If a platform doesn't respond within the legal window, escalation is automatic.
hiw.routing.title: Three ways a notice reaches the platform.
hiw.routing.sub: Different platforms accept notices differently. Asmita uses the most reliable channel that exists - and never guesses when one doesn't.
hiw.tier1.title: Grievance Officer email
hiw.tier1.body: For Indian intermediaries covered by IT Rules 2021, Asmita sends a templated email to the platform's designated Grievance Officer. This is the path most notices take.
hiw.tier2.title: Guided form handoff
hiw.tier2.body: When a platform has no published contact, Asmita does not guess. It prepares a step-by-step handoff so you can submit through their web form yourself, with the notice text ready to paste.
hiw.tier3.title: Direct API (coming soon)
hiw.tier3.body: For platforms that publish a verified takedown endpoint, Asmita will submit the notice through the API and wait on the structured response.
hiw.escalation.title: When platforms don't respond.
hiw.escalation.sub: The escalation timeline is automatic. You never have to chase a platform manually - but you can stop the clock at any time.
hiw.tl1.title: Notice sent.
hiw.tl1.body: First notice goes out the moment you approve it. The 24-hour clock under IT Rules begins.
hiw.tl2.title: First escalation.
hiw.tl2.body: If there is no response, Asmita escalates to the next contact tier and re-sends automatically.
hiw.tl3.title: FIR package ready.
hiw.tl3.body: If 7 days pass without resolution, Asmita prepares a police-ready FIR package for cybercrime.gov.in from the same evidence trail.
hiw.closing.title: Ready to begin?
hiw.closing.body: There is no clock running. You can start, stop, and come back.

faq.hero.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.hero.sub: Plain-language answers for survivors, supporters, NGOs, and reviewers.

faq.closing.body: Reach out before you start a case. We answer in English or Hindi - whichever is easier for you.
faq.s1.title: The basics
faq.s1.a1: Asmita is a privacy-first support platform for adults in India seeking help with non-consensual intimate-image abuse. It helps prepare platform notices under IT Rules 2021, track notice status, and preserve a clear audit trail - all without anyone at Asmita ever seeing your content.
faq.s1.q2: Does Asmita download or view submitted content?
faq.s1.a2: No. Asmita reads only the domain string from a submitted URL to identify which platform to contact. The link itself never reaches our server, and the content it points to is never fetched, opened, rendered, or stored. This is enforced at the architecture level, not just policy.
faq.s1.q3: Who can see the notice once it is sent?
faq.s1.a3: The grievance officer at the receiving platform receives a secure link to view the notice. That link is protected by a one-time password and burns after it is opened once - it cannot be revisited or forwarded. No one else at Asmita or outside it can access the notice content through that link.
faq.s1.a4: Yes. Notice templates are reviewed by a legal advisor before activation.
faq.s1.q5: What happens if a platform does not respond?
faq.s1.a5: The system schedules a follow-up at 24 hours and a re-send at 48 hours. If there is still no response after 7 days, Asmita prepares a police-ready FIR package for submission to cybercrime.gov.in.
faq.s2.title: Non-consensual intimate imagery
faq.s2.a1: Intimate images are images or videos showing nudity, underwear, genitals, sexual activity, or sexual poses. Deepfakes and AI-generated images that depict you in these ways are also included.
faq.s2.q2: Someone is threatening to share my images but hasn't posted them yet. Can Asmita help?
faq.s2.a2: Yes - this is called the preemptive or sextortion path, and it is fully supported. You can create a digital fingerprint of your images on your own device. That fingerprint, not the image, is included in legal notices to platforms so they can block the content before it is ever posted. Your images never leave your device.
faq.s2.q3: Someone else is also in the images. Can I still use Asmita?
faq.s2.a3: Yes. If you are in the image and it was shared without your consent, you can file a case regardless of who else appears in it.
faq.s2.a4: Yes. Sharing intimate images without consent is a criminal offence under the IT (Amendment) Act 2023 and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Platforms are also required under IT Rules 2021 to respond to takedown notices within 24 hours for such content. Asmita automates that notice process.
faq.s3.title: How image hashing works
faq.s3.a1: A digital fingerprint - technically called a PDQ hash - is a 64-character code generated from your image entirely on your own device. Only that code is sent to Asmita; the image itself never leaves your browser. Duplicate or near-duplicate copies of the same image produce the same fingerprint, so platforms can detect and block matching content without ever seeing the original. The algorithm cannot be run in reverse to recreate your image.
faq.s3.q2: Can the fingerprint be reversed to reveal my original image?
faq.s3.a2: No. Hashing is a one-way process. The fingerprint cannot be used to reconstruct or view your image by anyone - including Asmita, the platforms, or anyone who intercepts the notice.
faq.s3.q3: What if the image has been cropped, filtered, or edited?
faq.s3.a3: Each edited version produces a different fingerprint. If the version being circulated is cropped or filtered, you should generate a fingerprint from that version, not just the original. You can create multiple fingerprints - one for each meaningful variation.
faq.s3.q4: Can I delete the image from my device after the fingerprint is created?
faq.s3.a4: Yes. Once the fingerprint is generated, you can delete the image from your device. The fingerprint persists and will continue to work. It does not require the original image to remain.
faq.s3.q5: Does it work on deepfakes or AI-generated images?
faq.s3.a5: Yes. If a deepfake or AI-generated image depicts you in an intimate way, you can generate a fingerprint from it. Asmita treats synthetic intimate images the same as real ones.
faq.s4.title: Who can use Asmita, and what it can't do
faq.s4.a1: No. Minors are routed to CHILDLINE 1098, TakeItDown (NCMEC), and cybercrime.gov.in before any email or URL is collected. No case, session, or record is created. Content depicting anyone under 18 is governed by POCSO, which requires specialised handling that Asmita does not provide.
faq.s4.q2: Can I file on behalf of someone else?
faq.s4.a2: No - the case must be filed by the person depicted. This rule exists to prevent the tool from being used to target others. If you know someone who needs help, you can share Asmita with them and help them connect with a support organisation such as iCALL (9152987821).
faq.s4.q3: Does Asmita work for content shared on WhatsApp or Telegram private chats?
faq.s4.a3: No. These platforms use end-to-end encryption, which means content inside private chats cannot be detected or matched by any external tool. Asmita reaches platforms with public-facing content and verified grievance contacts. For encrypted-platform abuse, the National Cybercrime Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) is the right path.
faq.s4.q4: Does Asmita cover the whole internet?
faq.s4.a4: No. Asmita sends notices to platforms that have a verified grievance contact under IT Rules 2021. Personal websites, obscure hosting services, or platforms that ignore notices are beyond what Asmita can automatically resolve - in those cases the FIR package is the next step.
faq.s4.q5: What happens if the platform has no grievance officer contact?
faq.s4.a5: Asmita prepares a guided form handoff. The notice text, your PDQ fingerprint if applicable, and a direct link to the platform's own reporting form are all ready for you. You paste the text, submit the form yourself, and Asmita logs that submission in your case record.
faq.s4.q6: I don't have the original image anymore. Can I still file?
faq.s4.a6: For URL takedown, you don't need the image at all - just the link where the content appears. For digital fingerprinting, a high-quality screenshot can work if it is the best version you have access to.

minor.whyNot.title: The law treats this differently when a minor is involved.
minor.whyNot.body: In India, content showing anyone under 18 is treated under the POCSO Act, which carries mandatory reporting obligations and specialised handling. Sending you through an adult takedown flow would risk taking that protection away from you. That is why we route you here instead.
minor.closing.title: You are not alone in this.
minor.closing.body: Reach one of the lines above. They have helped many people in the situation you are in.

identity.hero.sub: Asmita does not ask for Aadhaar, PAN, or any government ID. The email you signed in with is the verified identity tied to every notice we send on your behalf.
identity.how.title: Three things, no documents.
identity.how.item1.rest: Each sign-in goes through a 6-digit code sent to your inbox.
identity.how.item2.rest: You confirm, under penalty of law, that the content is non-consensual and that you have the right to ask for its removal.
identity.how.item3.rest: Every action is logged with timestamp and a cryptographic hash chain, so the notices we send have a verifiable history.
identity.why.title: Collecting less is the safest design.
identity.why.body: Aadhaar tightens the identity link but introduces a category of data that becomes a target. Asmita deliberately refuses to collect it. Platforms that act under IT Rules 2021 do not require Aadhaar to process a takedown.

privacy.hero.sub: What Asmita collects, why, how long we keep it, who can see it, and what rights you have - in plain language.
privacy.tldr.title: Three promises that shape everything below.
privacy.tldr.p1.detail: URLs are read as domain strings only - the server never fetches the page. Image fingerprints are computed entirely on your device; only the 64-character hash code reaches us.
privacy.tldr.p2.detail: Asmita keeps notice metadata and case records, not the content the case is about.
privacy.tldr.p3.detail: No third party sees your case unless you explicitly route it there, or unless compelled by a court of law.

privacy.s01.p1: This policy applies to the Asmita platform - the website you are reading now, the case dashboard you sign in to with an email one-time-code, and any notices, evidence packages, or correspondence the platform produces on your behalf.
privacy.s01.p2: It does not cover the websites of any platform Asmita sends a takedown notice to, the cybercrime portal at cybercrime.gov.in, the Grievance Officers we email, or any third-party service you visit from a link in our pages. Those services have their own privacy policies.
privacy.s02.p1: Asmita is an India-specific platform built to help women remove non-consensual intimate content from the internet. It operates as a privacy-first notice and tracking service under the framework of the IT Rules 2021 and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
privacy.s02.p2: All enquiries should be sent to the Grievance Officer email listed in section 16.
privacy.s03.intro: The data Asmita stores can be divided into five categories. None of it is collected for marketing, profiling, or sale.
privacy.s03.i1.detail: Your email address (used only to send one-time login codes), and the timestamp of each sign-in. Asmita does not store passwords because Asmita does not use passwords.
privacy.s03.i2.detail: The URLs you submit (as text strings), the platform name detected from each URL, the digital declaration you sign when you create a case, any notes you choose to add, and PDQ fingerprint codes if you choose to submit them. PDQ hashes are 64-character codes generated on your device - the images are never sent to us. URLs and hash codes are stored encrypted at rest.
privacy.s03.i3.detail: The text of the takedown notices we send on your behalf, the timestamps of each delivery attempt, and the contents of any reply the platform sends to our handling address.
privacy.s03.i4.detail: Limited server logs that record IP address, user-agent, request path, status code, and timestamp - used for abuse detection and security incident review. These are kept for 30 days and then automatically purged.
privacy.s04.intro: Some things Asmita refuses to collect by design - meaning the architecture would have to be re-built before it could ever start collecting them.
privacy.s04.i1.detail: We do not request, fetch, render, download, proxy, cache, thumbnail, transcode, or otherwise interact with the media behind any URL you share. URLs are opaque text tokens - the server only reads the domain string. PDQ fingerprinting uses a client-side algorithm: the image is processed in your browser, and only the resulting 64-character code is transmitted. Our servers never receive, store, or process the image file itself. A network-level monitor blocks outbound requests to any submitted URL host as a further defence.
privacy.s04.i2.detail: Authentication is by email one-time code only.
privacy.s04.i3.bold: Aadhaar, PAN, or any government ID.
privacy.s04.i3.detail: Asmita does not collect, request, or accept Aadhaar offline-XML bundles, PAN cards, or any other government identity document. The email you sign in with is the verified identity tied to your case.
privacy.s04.i4.bold: Tracking pixels, advertising identifiers, or cross-site cookies.
privacy.s05.intro: Each piece of data exists because a specific feature would not work without it.
privacy.s05.i1.detail: to authenticate you (one-time codes), to send case status updates, and to receive replies from platforms on your behalf.
privacy.s05.i2.detail: to identify which platform each notice is addressed to, to compose the notice, and to record what was sent for your audit trail.
privacy.s05.i2b.detail: to include in notices so that platforms can identify and proactively block matching content. The code is shared only with platforms you address a notice to.
privacy.s05.i3.detail: to satisfy the legal requirement that the person filing the notice declares ownership of the rights, under penalty of law.
privacy.s05.i4.detail: to detect abuse of the platform, to investigate security incidents, and to meet auditability requirements.
privacy.s06.p1a: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act), Asmita processes your data on the basis of your
privacy.s06.p1b: , which you give at registration and again at the point of each case creation. The consent is purpose-specific - agreeing to create a case does not consent to anything outside of preparing and routing the takedown notice you ask for.
privacy.s06.p2a: For the limited operational logs described in section 3, Asmita relies on
privacy.s06.p2b: under Section 7 of the DPDP Act, restricted to security and abuse prevention. These logs are not used for any other purpose.
privacy.s07.intro: The retention schedule below is enforced by automated jobs. Times are measured from the date the relevant event ends (case resolution, account deletion, log creation).
privacy.s07.i1.detail: kept while the case is open and for 90 days after resolution, so you have time to download your audit trail and FIR package.
privacy.s07.i2.detail: kept until you delete your account.
privacy.s07.i3.detail: soft delete is immediate. A scheduled job permanently erases the account and all linked case data 30 days after soft delete, unless you have an open legal hold.
privacy.s07.i5.detail: kept indefinitely for platform-response statistics and accountability reporting. These contain no personal data.
privacy.s08.intro: Asmita shares your data only in the narrow circumstances listed below. We do not sell data. We do not exchange data with advertisers, data brokers, or social-media platforms outside the takedown notice itself.
privacy.s08.i1.bold: Platforms, when you send a notice.
privacy.s08.i1.detail: The notice contains the URLs you submitted, the platform name, your declaration text, any PDQ hash codes, and the contact email you authorised. Nothing else. The grievance officer receives the notice via a secure link protected by a one-time password. That link burns after it is opened once and cannot be revisited or forwarded.
privacy.s08.i2.detail: We disclose data to a law-enforcement agency only on receipt of a valid order under Indian law. We will attempt to notify you unless legally prohibited.
privacy.s08.i3.bold: NGO partners, only when you ask.
privacy.s08.i3.detail: If you choose to vouch through an NGO partner, the NGO sees only what you authorise it to see for that vouching action.
privacy.s08.i4.detail: Asmita uses managed infrastructure for database, email delivery, and hosting. These providers process data under written agreements.
privacy.s09.intro: Security is a stack of overlapping controls. None of them is perfect alone; together they make compromise expensive.
privacy.s09.i1.detail: All data at rest is encrypted at the disk layer. Sensitive fields - submitted URLs, declaration text - are also encrypted at the application layer with per-case keys.
privacy.s09.i2.detail: Application servers run inside a private network with no outbound access except for the specific platform endpoints needed for notice delivery.
privacy.s09.i3.detail: Email one-time codes only, with rate limits on requests and on URL submissions (10 URLs per 24 hours per account).
privacy.s09.i4.detail: All state-changing requests are CSRF-protected. Session cookies are HTTP-only, Secure, and SameSite-Lax.
privacy.s09.i5.detail: Every access to sensitive data by an administrator is recorded in an append-only security event log.
privacy.s09.i6.detail: A live integrity check verifies that the application does not make outbound HTTP requests to user-submitted URLs. If it ever did, alerting fires immediately.
privacy.s10.intro: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 gives you a set of rights over your own data. Asmita honours each of them without charge.
privacy.s10.i1.detail: You can download every piece of data we hold about you, at any time, from your case dashboard.
privacy.s10.i2.detail: You can edit your email address, declaration text, and any free-text fields in your case. URL submissions can be withdrawn but not edited (so the audit trail stays sound).
privacy.s10.i3.detail: You can delete your account at any time. After a 30-day soft-delete window - during which you can restore - the data is permanently erased.
privacy.s10.i4.detail: You can write to the Grievance Officer listed in section 16. We acknowledge every grievance within 72 hours and resolve or escalate within 14 days.
privacy.s10.i5.detail: You can nominate another person to exercise these rights on your behalf in case of incapacity or death. Contact the Grievance Officer to set this up.
privacy.s11.p1: Asmita does not knowingly collect any personal data from a person under the age of 18. The age attestation at the start of every case flow routes anyone who indicates they are under 18 away from URL submission and into a curated set of child-safety resources, including CHILDLINE 1098, TakeItDown (NCMEC), and cybercrime.gov.in.
privacy.s11.p2: If we learn that we have collected data from a minor through an inaccurate attestation, that data is deleted immediately and the case account is closed. Concerned parents or guardians can write to the Grievance Officer.
privacy.s12.p1: Asmita uses two cookies, both strictly functional: a session cookie that keeps you signed in, and a language-preference cookie that remembers whether you chose English or Hindi. No third-party advertising, marketing, or tracking cookies are set by Asmita.
privacy.s12.p2: Asmita does not use Google Analytics, Facebook Pixel, or any equivalent third-party analytics suite. Aggregate platform-response statistics are computed from internal logs that contain no personal data.
privacy.s13.p1: Asmita is built for India. All personal data is stored on servers physically located in India. The list of sub-processors is maintained in our public sub-processor register and updated whenever the list changes.
privacy.s13.p2: We do not transfer your data outside India, except where a specific platform you have asked us to send a notice to is located outside India - in which case the notice itself (and only the notice) crosses the border.
privacy.s14.p1: If a personal-data breach occurs that is likely to result in risk to you, we will notify the Data Protection Board of India and the affected users without undue delay, in accordance with the DPDP Act. The notification will include the nature of the breach, the data affected, the likely consequences, and the steps we have taken to contain it.
privacy.s14.p2: Even when not legally required, we will notify you of any incident that affected your case data.
privacy.s15.p1: We will post any change to this policy at this URL, with a new "Last updated" date at the top. For material changes - anything that expands what we collect, broadens with whom we share, or lengthens retention - we will give you at least 30 days advance notice by email before the change takes effect.
privacy.s16.p1: The Grievance Officer is the named human responsible for replying to your privacy questions and grievances.
privacy.s16.p2b: with the subject line "Privacy grievance", or use the
privacy.s16.p3: A full legal opinion is on file.
privacy.closing.title: Privacy is the architecture.
privacy.closing.sub: If anything on this page is unclear, write to us. We will answer in English or Hindi - whichever is easier for you.
